The first is “Naughty,” Olivia Wilde’s raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer […]
articles.content:
Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros . Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety .

The first is “ Naughty ,” Olivia Wilde’s raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer Aniston. The other is “ Nasty ,” Mary Bronstein’s psychological drama led by Jenna Ortega, which will roll out under Warner’s new indie label Clockwork. Universal slated “Naughty” for Nov. 5, 2027, after registering the name with the Motion Picture Association in 2023, according to two sources. Clockwork, the nascent shingle run by Neon veteran Christian Parkes, has not officially set a date for “Nasty,” though four sources say the film is also eyeing a November 2027 release. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘PAW Patrol’ Spinoff Series ‘Skye’s Pup Squad’ Set for 2027 Release

Generally, studios go to great lengths to avoid delivering movies with similar-sounding names — much less launching them in the same corridor. “Naughty” and “Nasty” aren’t alike in genre or subject matter. “Naughty,” featuring Aniston and Peter Dinklage, follows a single mom who has to convince Santa Claus to testify at her divorce hearing. “Nasty,” Bronstein’s follow-up to “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You,” revolves around an elite gymnast competing for a spot on the Olympic team while dealing with her manipulative coach.

Yet insiders at Universal and Warner Bros. feel the fact that the titles are basically synonyms could confuse moviegoers. Further complicating the matter is that LuckyChap, Margot Robbie’s prolific film and TV production shop, is backing both projects. Universal and Clockwork declined to comment. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The spat is headed toward a formal review by the MPA, which has a 101-year-old department called the Title Registration Bureau to manage such conflicts. Arbitration involves a panel of studio intellectual property lawyers at the ready to hash it out. Although titles are not copyrightable, the TRB is armed with a 50-page document outlining rules of play and precedent, per one source, and its rulings are legally binding. The MPA declined to comment on the matter.

"Movies want to distinguish themselves, and the first way they do that is the title," says Jeff Bock, an analyst with Exhibitor Relations. "If they sound similar, there could be confusion."

Universal believes it should have dibs since it was first to file with “Naughty.” That would mean “Nasty” either changes its name or shifts its release date. Insiders note Clockwork filed two alternative titles for “Nasty” with its MPA documentation, but the filmmakers are against using the backups.

Meanwhile, sources close to “Nasty” feel that Universal is “punching down” at Clockwork because the indie drama doesn’t have the same broad commercial appeal as the Aniston-led holiday comedy. (Though Clockwork is a specialty label, it is owned and operated by the vast Skydance Motion Picture Group). Wilde is content to let “Nasty” proceed as titled, according to a person familiar with her thinking. LuckyChap is working toward a solution that sets up both projects for success without entering MPA arbitration, two sources add.

Disputes like these rarely become public knowledge, insiders say. And most often, studios work it out without involving the Title Registration Bureau. The group’s last two arbitrations were in 2018. That’s when Disney and Lucasfilm settled on “Solo: A Star Wars Story” rather than “Solo” to distinguish the Han Solo origin story from the 2018 climbing documentary “Free Solo.” And Universal agreed to change its raunchy comedy to “Blockers” from “The Pact,” a name that was already used by a 2012 horror film.

Renaming movies can benefit both parties. Ask Paramount and Sony, which released “No Strings Attached” and “Friends With Benefits” a few months apart in 2011. Both romantic comedies — one starring Natalie Portman and Ashton Kutcher and the other with Mila Kunis and Justin Timberlake — had an identical premise involving two friends who agree to casual sex without dating. “No Strings Attached” was originally called “Friends With Benefits,” but the studio acquiesced to the title change. Any plot similarities didn't dilute the films’ respective box office, with each one grossing $149 million globally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

To that end, movies with similar themes or ideas are less of a problem for studios. Bock points to 1998’s “Armageddon” and “Deep Impact,” two disaster films about comets on a collision course with Earth. Both were theatrical winners, with “Armageddon” earning $553 million globally and “Deep Impact” generating $350 million globally.

“Consumers might be fooled by something like that, but it didn’t affect the box office," he says. "They turned out to be different, even though the synopsis was the same."

articles.title: Montel Williams Gets Candid About the State of Daytime TV: "The Talk Shows of My Era Became the Reality Shows of Today"
articles.summary: The former 'Montel Williams Show' host talks about how short attention spans have changed the daytime talk show landscape during a conversation on the 'We're Out of Time' podcast with host Richard Taite.
articles.content:
Montel Williams is getting candid about the state of daytime talk show, saying viewers' attention spans have changed a lot since he ended his own talker in 2008.

"It's a sad commentary that we lost our attention span in the last 15 years," he said in a conversation with We’re Out of Time podcast host Richard Taite, debuting Tuesday. "The talk shows that I did and the talk shows of that era were hourlong talk discussions. We don't have the patience anymore to listen to a topic for an hour. I say the majority of people don't." Related Stories TV 'Property Brother' Jonathan Scott Is Getting a Daytime Talk Show TV Montel Williams Hospitalized After Workout, Spokesman Says

He said the format has morphed quite a bit since his show ended. ( The Montel Williams Show ran from July 1991 to May 2008, spanning 17 seasons.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"So the talk shows of my era became the reality shows of today," he opined. "I'll say that again, the talk shows of my era became the reality shows of today. We took the dysfunction that we put on display and turned those into individual shows of their own, to the point now that the talk that's out there right now, what do they really even talk? Other than selling products and hawking a new movie or hawking a new record, what do they do? Is there any discussion that makes man better?"

Williams was quick to say he's not criticizing anyone in particular, just nothing how times have changed.

"I'm not casting aspersion on my peers of the day," he said. "But I am saying that at least back when we talked about issues, we talked about issues that changed the world, that I believe changed America. We were talking about AIDS before any news stations were going full reports on it. We were talking about civil unrest, we were talking about racism, we were talking about hate, we were talking about all those things that we didn't even talk about it around the dinner table. We talked about it. Some of us did it in the salacious way. But at least they had a discussion." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Williams added that the goal with his show was to educate people and put a spotlight on a topic that viewers perhaps hadn't been introduced to or thought that much about. In other words, something that would "make you stop and think," he said.

Does he think that kind of talk show would work today?

"It could, if it was formatted differently," he says. "I think we can go an entire hour, but we have to go in that hour introducing every single piece of that topic, not just one piece, but we have to introduce it all and add to it information that people can take away."

Taite likened that to scrolling on your phone, where you're staying engaged by absorbing different information — and a lot of it — in a short time span.

"That's right, and [keeping] you stimulated on the same topic instead of scrolling, or swiping up and down, instead of doing that and getting a different topic every single second, and that's what they're trying to do," Williams replied. "They're trying to give you something different every five or six minutes where they never really even solved the first five minutes. I say that every single topic out there can be broken into 20 different topics. Somebody needs to just program it that way."

He added, “I think we may gravitate back to that as soon as we realize that we pushed attention span to a point where it's no longer attention span.”

The full episode of We’re Out of Time with Montel Williams and host Richard Taite premieres at noon PT on Tuesday on YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you have ever wanted to say "Not today, Satan" in Grand Theft Auto , Rockstar Games has made that dream possible in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Given that the studio has never been shy about embracing the weird side , this inclusion isn't surprising and fits right into that tradition. With this mission, players can follow Jason and Lucia into the depths of Hell and battle the Devil and his army of demons. This may take the cake as far as supernatural encounters go, in both Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption .

Many of the series best discoveries come from ridiculous encounters like this , and Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't disappoint. This latest discovery in GTA 6 takes things considerably further and fits right in with the infamous Mount Chiliad mystery in Grand Theft Auto 5 and the unsettling secrets scattered throughout Red Dead Redemption 2 . But the best part of battling the Devil in this GTA 6 secret is the reward: exclusive cosmetics, a powerful shotgun, and a permanent character upgrade that makes the mission worth seeking out. But the question remains: how do you get to Hell and fight Satan in GTA 6 ?

Players looking to fight the Devil in Grand Theft Auto 6 will need to head to Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. The secret mission is accessible during Chapter 2, and players can complete it as either Jason or Lucia. However, there are some specific conditions players must meet before they can descend into Hell. Simply visiting the location during the middle of the day won't follow the recommended method for triggering the encounter. Instead, you must follow a set of guidelines shared below.

Following this sequence transports your character to Hell, where you fight an army of demons. You'll find yourself equipped with a special shotgun that makes dealing with these demonic forces easier, and eventually you'll come face-to-face with the Devil. Satan is a tough foe and will summon demons as backup, so be sure to eliminate these when they appear. Be sure to collect the Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun beside Satan's throne before leaving Hell.

After defeating Satan, players will awaken back at the campsite. Completing this hidden GTA 6 mission offers the Circles of Hell clothing top, a new tattoo design, the aforementioned shotgun, and a permanent health increase. The cosmetics are great, but the weapon and upgrade are the best rewards and make this mission a must-play.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of Easter eggs and secrets like this, and players will likely be uncovering them for years. For now, the Devil stands out as one of the more unique missions in Vice City.

The story centers the pair, two senior editors competing to oust the other from a condensed role due to impending layoffs, chasing big book deals for the publishing […]
articles.content:
Clashing Through the Snow director Carlson Young found it easy to relate to the film’s two main characters, Ryan Mitchell ( Christopher Briney ) and Hannah Hendricks ( Michelle Randolph ).

The story centers the pair, two senior editors competing to oust the other from a condensed role due to impending layoffs, chasing big book deals for the publishing company where they work. Ryan operates off of commercial motivation and tapping into what is popular to sell books while Hannah identifies as more of a literary purist who takes big swings with the depth of books she takes on.

“[The script] really spoke to me. I felt so connected to Hannah and Ryan's literary perspectives, and it felt like a existential conversation that I have with myself, moment to moment, constantly,” Young told Deadline. “It was easy for me to access their personalities and their inner worlds. And then I just loved the classic, holiday hijinks that ensue from there, and I was up for the challenge of trying to make a great holiday rom-com.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The director connected the differing stances on what sells to challenges she navigates in her own job “balancing art and commerce, and what is and isn't viable in storytelling and in the marketplace."

“It is true that publishing and cinemas, these are tectonically shifting industries, and trying to find yourself your voice either as a book editor or director, whatever you're doing, it doesn't even need to be in a creative field,” she added. “But we're all existing in these shifting sands, and so that was my way in. That's why I was looking at it like that.”

In the below interview, Young unpacks specific moments like Lukas Gage’s “scene stealer” appearance, the Buc-ee’s knockoff Luc-ee's, Ryan’s seeking advice by talking to ChatGPT and more.

DEADLINE: I spoke with Chris and Michelle earlier, and they mentioned you gave Chris a note comparing him to Jim Carrey. Did you have any other references? Could you expand on that? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

CARLSON YOUNG: When we were rehearsing, I kept looking at him and seeing this physical comedy coming to the surface, and I was like, "This is like some Jim Carrey. I love this for you. Go off on that." We tweaked it and trimmed it and shaped it in the edit, but he's really funny. I hope that he does a lot more comedy.

DEADLINE: What was your role in the Luc-ee’s knockoff to Buc-ee’s?

YOUNG: I don't know what I can and can't say about Buc-ee’s/ Luc-ee's, but we did our best. We did our version. I'm from Texas, Buc-ee's is a big part of the psychology of a Texan, and so it was really funny, and we did our own version of it.

DEADLINE: For the part where Hannah's in the helicopter venting to the pilot and Ryan's driving the truck talking to AI, was there ever a plan to have him talking to a person or was it always going to be ChatGPT?

YOUNG: I have to say, yes, there was [a different iteration]. I personally thought that him talking to Chat was so Ryan. It made me laugh so much. And the amount of times that I've caught my husband… I'm like, ‘Are you asking ChatGPT a question? Like for real? Are you serious? ‘And he is serious. It just felt really modern and so of the times, and something like his character would actually do. And I like a lot the responses that Chat has for him. It just made me laugh.

DEADLINE: Lukas Gage is so funny in the small role he plays. He had a similar comedic presence in People We Meet on Vacation . How did you want to incorporate him in the storyline?

YOUNG: He's a scene-stealer. You just give him an inch, and he will create a million miles of gold. He's a spinster. And when we Facetimed about the character, he had the funniest ideas and instincts on it, like 'He's like Chris Elliott in Scary Movie ." I absolutely loved that. "That's our north star. Let's go do that.” He's such a breath of fresh air once they get to the Mercyville Inn, and he's such a phenomenal human. We'll see him in, like, 100 more movies.

DEADLINE: Where did you shoot? Ryan and Hannah come from LA, but they get to New York on a road trip. How did you balance the different locations?

YOUNG: We shot in New York, a bit in the city, a bit upstate. We were shooting the Hudson Valley as you know Indiana and Colorado and Utah and it definitely lent itself. We were also experiencing historic winter weather in New York, like blizzards and production shut down. Many a hurdle, and so it was truly 'Clashing Through the Snow.' We had a big snow budget, and we didn't have to use it because it was just snow everywhere.

DEADLINE: Did the snow budget get redirected to other things?

YOUNG: Absolutely, girl. Our producers would have something to say about that.

DEADLINE: My mind goes to the music, which Prime Video is always good at getting, but the Olivia Rodrigo songs specifically…

YOUNG: That’s how we got the Olivia Rodrigo song. I like that story. I think we should go with that. We saved on snow, so we got this incredible Olivia Rodrigo song.

DEADLINE: Not only “Begged” in the film but “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)” was in the trailer.

YOUNG: I love her song in the film as well. We’re super lucky to have her.

DEADLINE: You’ve done Upgraded with Prime Video as well as The Last Sunrise . articles.title: Cyclops Star Confirms Avengers: Doomsday Will Do Something Never Seen in the X-Men Films
articles.summary: Disney - Marvel The inclusion of many characters from the Fox era of X-Men movies is one of the most interesting aspects of Avengers: Doomsday, but the real treat is getting to see a fresh attempt at getting Cyclops right. While those Fox X-Men films did a lot of things right and fans still fondly remember them, most […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The inclusion of many characters from the Fox era of X-Men movies is one of the most interesting aspects of Avengers: Doomsday , but the real treat is getting to see a fresh attempt at getting Cyclops right. While those Fox X-Men films did a lot of things right and fans still fondly remember them, most people agree that th e handling of Scott Summers, aka Cyclops, was a problem . Despite having a notable actor in James Marsden in the role, the movies didn't prioritize the character, which was hugely disappointing to fans who fell in love with Cyclops on the pages of the comic book and in X-Men: The Animated Series .

Thankfully, James Marsden is back as Cyclops in Avengers: Doomsday and has announced that we will finally see his version of the character done right. Rather than being used purely as a pawn in a love triangle with Wolverine and Jean Grey , this big-screen take on Cyclops will showcase him as what he truly is at heart, which is a leader. It's exactly what many of us have wanted from Scott Summers in a movie, especially after seeing the character handled so well recently in the X-Men '97 animated series.

While promoting the epic blockbuster Avengers: Doomsday , James Marsden spoke with Sharp Magazine . They talked about what made him return to the role, especially since many would agree that the character was handled so poorly in the past. He talked with Marvel Studios and the Russo Brothers, who wanted to take an authentic approach to Cyclops, which includes showing him as a leader. Marsden didn't want this return to just be a small cameo, which he had already done at the end of X-Men: Days of Future Past .

"One of the things people have said for years is that Cyclops is a leader, yet in many of the previous films he often took a back seat to Wolverine and some of the other characters," Marsden said. "There are only so many minutes available in a film this large, but it was important to me that my return felt meaningful." The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday just released and seems to cement the idea that Cyclops will play a major role. He is shown fighting with Sam Wilson before delivering the iconic " To me, my X-Men " line as various heroes drop in alongside him.

Getting Cyclops right is important to fix the way he was done in the past, but it's also crucial to set up the future of the MCU. We already know that Kit Connor has been cast as Scott Summers in the upcoming X-Men film in 2028. If Avengers: Doomsday can give us a great Cyclops, it'll set up Scott as a true leader for the future . James Marsden certainly seems happy with what's to come in Avengers: Doomsday , adding, "I didn’t want Cyclops to simply appear for a nostalgic cameo and then disappear. I wanted there to be a genuine purpose behind his presence. Without giving anything away, I feel very good about what we were able to do with the character."

Avengers: Doomsday has to get several major things right, from establishing Doctor Doom to balancing so many characters to likely setting the table for Avengers: Secret Wars . Giving us a proper Cyclops on the big screen ranks right alongside those as it can impact the past of the X-Men and its future.

articles.title: Bleach's Hell Arc Deserves to Return With New Sequel

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its official anime run earlier this Fall to cap over 22 years of the anime franchise. This adapted the final […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's still one final Bleach arc that's left to tell its story, and fans deserve to see it come to fruition one day to continue from Tite Kubo's original series. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War ended its official anime run earlier this Fall to cap over 22 years of the anime franchise . This adapted the final arc of Kubo's original manga, but that's also far from the end of the story as it is. Because back in 2021, Kubo actually continued from that finale to start something new.

When Bleach was celebrating its 20th anniversary, that's where it was first announced that the anime would be returning for a proper adaptation of Kubo's final arc. But that wasn't all as Kubo himself also came back to the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump with a new one-shot picking up from the original end of the story. Featuring an older Ichigo Kurosaki, introducing new characters, enemies and more, Bleach' s Hell Arc really needs to be fleshed out with a full sequel.

Bleach "No Breathes From Hell" was a 75 page one-shot manga release that first launched in 2021, and picks up a few years after the original end of the series. Exploring more of the ten year time skip seen with the original finale, Kazui and Ichika have grown a bit older and more of the Soul Society rankings have filled out with the new one-shot introducing some new members to each squad. Kazui has grown much stronger, and the Soul Society is preparing for a special bit of funeral rites for the late Ukitake. But things get more complicated from there.

A massive skeletal being arrives with no one other than Ichika being able to sense it before it makes its move, and it's revealed that these new monsters don't have any spiritual pressure of their own. Soon enough, the formerly defeated Szayelaporro arrives and reveals that he was cast into Hell after his defeat. It's a brand new region that has never been referenced before, and with it has granted him an entirely new level of dark power that seems to have given him godly new abilities.

Soul Society begins to get covered in a dark matter known as "Phosphoplasm" and an entire new class of beings is revealed. Beings with too strong spiritual pressure never return completely to the Soul Society and are said to have been sent somewhere else and thus cast into Hell. This includes former enemies and even former Soul Reapers that have died in battle. With the final pages of the one shot, Bleach kicks off the "New Breathes From Hell" arc with no signs of continuing after five long years.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War' s anime finale has now put a final button on the story, but this one-shot remains a continuation that has yet to be touched even after five years of inactivity. This new sequel teases returns from not only some of those most memorable villains of the past, but also new and terrifying versions of each of the major fan favorite Soul Reapers that have died along the way. There's even a potential to see some of the Soul Reapers that had never been even shown until they were teased in the anime like the first generation of fighters .

But after spending all this time to bring back Bleach through the anime, and even having Kubo continue the franchise's story with a new one-shot and even the Burn the Witch spinoff series, there's clearly an interest from the creator to keep messing around with the story . A new sequel would be the perfect way to keep it going, but there are also other potential issues that spring up as a result. That includes the potential schedule for which Kubo would need to abide by. That probably seems like the biggest hurdle to overcome, but not an impossible one.

Shueisha's editorial department has worked with their notable creators before to work out a schedule that's for the creators' benefit like seen with Hunter x Hunter' s Yoshihiro Togashi. They've already done that with Kubo's work on Burn the Witch, so it's possible that they could work out a new schedule that could allow this sequel to exist. Where it's a big chapter coming out every few months, weekly, or even once a year, Bleach just needs to continue so we can see what's next . Would you want to see more of Bleach' s Hell Arc? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Francis Lawrence Signed On for One 'Hunger Games' Movie. Five Films Later, He's the Keeper of Panem
articles.summary: The 'Sunrise on the Reaping' director looks back on the pressure of taking over a franchise, his decade-long collaboration with Suzanne Collins, why the series endures, and where things stand on ‘Constantine 2’ and 'Red Rising.'
articles.content:
The morning after the New York premiere of The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping , Francis Lawrence is still taking in the view from the night before.

On one red carpet stood nearly every era of Panem. There were the newcomers: Joseph Zada , Whitney Peak and Mckenna Grace, along with franchise first-timers Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes and Glenn Close. Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Josh Andrés Rivera who starred in Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes prequel, were in attendance. And there were the originals, Jennifer Lawrence , Josh Hutcherson , Woody Harrelson , Elizabeth Banks, Jena Malone and Willow Shields assembled like the franchise's own Avengers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies New 'Hunger Games' Movie on the Way? Lionsgate Film Chief Shares Latest on Franchise's Future Beyond the Book 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians': How Season 3 Brings Epic Moments to Life and Deals With Annabeth's Absence in the Books

"Last night at the premiere, for the first time, we had three generations of cast," Lawrence tells The Hollywood Reporter of the Nov. 16 event. "There's something really special about the time we've all spent together and the quality of people I've gotten to work with."

Lawrence has been a constant across all of them. Since taking over from director Gary Ross with 2013's Catching Fire , he has directed every Hunger Games film that followed, working alongside producer Nina Jacobson to turn Suzanne Collins' dystopian saga following teenagers forced into fatal combat into one of Hollywood's most dependable franchises. The original four films grossed roughly $2.98 billion worldwide, and Collins' five books have sold more than 100 million copies globally, growing into one of the most successful young adult publishing franchises in history.

Still, the scale didn't fully hit him until the final Mockingjay films. Around the release of the films, The Hunger Games: The Exhibition opened to fans, and Lawrence walked through it with his stars. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Walking through it for the first time with Jen and Josh, and I think Liam [Hemsworth] was there, we were all just stunned that we had made something museum-worthy, with our music, our costumes, our props, pieces of our sets and the lore," he recalls. "There's something really special in that, knowing these stories have connected with people in a certain way."

Amid the success, it's easy to forget that Lawrence arrived in Panem as an outsider. He had never made a sequel to someone else's first film, and on Catching Fire he was "joining an existing family," with a cast "so big and so seasoned" that he felt he had a lot to prove. He also assumed it would be a one-time job.

"The weird thing is, when I signed on to Catching Fire , I thought that was going to be the only one I did," he says.

Instead, the studio asked him to stay for the two-part Mockingjay . "A huge part of me is very appreciative of being invited to keep making these movies and be part of this team."

That invitation, however, came with a nerve-racking stretch. A few weeks into shooting Mockingjay , production paused for a month so Lawrence and the team could promote and release Catching Fire . He would face its box office verdict with most of the next film's shoot still ahead of him.

"Man, what if this thing bombs?" he remembers thinking of the pressure for Catching Fire success amid filming the third installment. "I now still have like 125 days of shooting with all of these people that are going to be looking at me like, 'We just made a movie with this guy that bombed.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He needn't have worried. After its 2013 release, Catching Fire became the franchise's highest grossing film, and the once outsider became the keeper of the series. "The series was quite popular at that point, and there was a lot of excitement and confidence at the studio, so that was nice," he says.

When Lawrence and Jacobson returned eight years later with 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , the odds felt less certain. The prequel had no Katniss and centered on the rise of the tyrant Coriolanus Snow, played by Donald Sutherland in the original films with Tom Blyth taking on the role for a younger version.

"A bunch of time had gone by, and you wonder if there's still an appetite for Hunger Games , especially Hunger Games without Katniss," he says. "It had a very different structure, and it was a story about the person everybody hates, so a lot of things made me a little nervous."

Sunrise on the Reaping , which traces the origins of the fan-favorite mentor Haymitch Abernathy, felt different.

"Weirdly, this one I kind of felt less pressure," Lawrence says. "I felt much more confident that this was one that fans really wanted to see, and it felt like a return to form for movies like Catching Fire and the original."

There being a new Hunger Games book came as a surprise to Lawrence, who assures he, along with Jacobson, are just as in the dark as everyone else. After more than a decade of working together, Lawrence and Collins have a routine. She keeps quiet while she writes, and only once her publisher confirms she has a book does she bring in Lawrence and Jacobson, always with the same modest question of whether the story is a movie. Lawrence and Jacobson always say yes. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Sunrise , Lawrence and Jacobson got word of the novel earlier than ever, and the secrecy was tighter as a result. The manuscript was kept at Collins‘ agent's home, and then then moved to a locked safe kept with Jacobson. Screenwriter Billy Ray wrote on an offline laptop in Jacobson's office, while Lawrence stayed busy making secret trips to read it.

"This one we got further in advance, while she was still going back and forth with her editors," he says. "I had read it a couple of times, Nina had read it a couple of times, and I went to New York to work with Suzanne on breaking down the book into what we thought the movie would be. We hired [original screenwriter] Billy Ray. He was already writing and we were having calls about the draft. So a lot of work was done before the book was even announced, and I couldn't talk to anybody about it."

The book and its film adaptation were announced together in June 2024, which brought "a lot of relief,” he says. "At least then people knew we were working on it and that it was the Haymitch story. We just had to keep quiet about the storyline itself.”

That left the biggest challenge: finding a young Haymitch, the carefree kid from District 12 long before he became the drunken, broken mentor Harrelson made iconic. The search led to Zada, the breakout from Prime Video's We Were Liars and Netflix's East of Eden . Lawrence put him "through the wringer" in auditions before landing on the actor to carry the beloved character's origin story. The seeds for the origin story were "planted over twenty years ago" when Collins began the original trilogy, the author reflected in a letter s hared on social media amid the release of Sunrise . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Collins praised Zada's performance as "remarkably powerful and moving."

Long before he was steering a multibillion-dollar franchise, Lawrence spent years making some of the most memorable music videos of the MTV era for artists like Britney Spears, Lady Gaga, Justin Timberlake and Jennifer Lopez. He doesn't think much about those days when he's making a movie, he says, but their influence is still there nearly 20 years later.

"Having done maybe around 120 videos, it gave me a playground to learn the toolkit I have for making things look a certain way," Lawrence says. "I got to create different worlds, try different things, learn about visual effects and learn about working with performers. So in terms of visual style, I just had confidence in the image in general: if I imagine something, how can I actually make that happen? Because of videos, that became second nature, so I could focus more on performance and story. That's probably the biggest way it's affected my moviemaking in general."

It's fitting, then, that music runs through Panem. The films have long used it to amplify their themes of resistance. Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss sings "The Hanging Tree," which became a rebel anthem. In the prequels, Zegler's Lucy Gray Baird and Peak's Lenore Dove are both musicians who capture the hearts of Snow and Haymitch.

Lawrence approaches that music the way he approached his videos: "much more music-forward than lyrics-forward." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I take the mood, tone and feel of a song, and most of the ideas I built for my videos were based on the mood of the song rather than the lyrics. Not always, but I'd say 90 percent of the time. It's the same here: I'm primarily thinking about the mood, tone and emotional value of music and what I want something to feel like," he explains.

Music is also common ground with Collins. "She's a real music aficionado with a library in her head, and I had long conversations with her and with [executive music producer and songwriter] Dave Cobb about the creation of songs. She [Collins] usually has a historical background for why and how she wrote certain things, and I would talk to Dave, our music producer, mostly about how I wanted songs to feel. So whether it's 'The Hanging Tree,' a Covey song or 'The Old Therebefore,' it's really about mood," he says.

The music doesn't stop when the cameras roll. "I also listen to a lot of music when I shoot," Lawrence says. "Often I'll be watching a scene with music I have as inspiration playing in my ear, whether it's score from our movies or from other movies, because I'm evoking a mood, a tone and an emotional value I want to feel in the scene. So sometimes I'm listening to dialogue and to music on my phone at the same time."

His usual choices: The franchise's scores, of which there are five movies worth, and "Lily's Theme," Alexandre Desplat's piece from Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 .

"That has always felt very Hunger Games -ish to me," he says of the Potter score. "I also listened to some more disturbing stuff for this one, because I thought of it as a bit scarier. Instead of listening to action-oriented music during fight sequences, I'd listen to things that are a little more disturbing and scary. So it was kind of all over the place.“ blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Building worlds became Lawrence's calling card when he made the leap to features. His 2005 debut, Constantine , was a dark take on the DC Comics antihero, and he followed it by envisioning a New York City post-plague for the Will Smith hit I Am Legend (2007). Then came the Great Depression-era romance Water for Elephants (2011), a reunion with Jennifer Lawrence on the spy thriller Red Sparrow (2018), and more recently Slumberland (2022) and the Stephen King adaptation The Long Walk (2025).

The genres vary, but in hindsight, the dystopian streak running through several of them looks a lot like a rehearsal for the road to the Panem Capitol. Amid revisiting Hunger Games in the prequels, the director says he's "trying to" return to where it all began with his first feature, Constantine . It was announced in 2022 that Lawrence would helm a sequel with star Keanu Reeves reprising his role and Akiva Goldsman writing the script. "We have a script," Lawrence confirms.

Part of the appeal of a sequel is getting the band back together. The other part is unfinished business with the ratings board, and this time Lawrence wants to lean into the R rating he once tried to avoid.

"We got saddled with an R rating even though we followed all the PG-13 rules, and that was a tough blow," he says. "On Hunger Games, every time I turn in a cut, it's an R, we go back and forth a little, and we get to PG-13. With Constantine , they said, 'We've stopped taking notes. There's no getting a PG-13 on this movie.' So we were stuck. Part of it was: let's make another one because we enjoyed it, but this time let's make the hard-R version. If we're going to get an R, let's make the R-rated Constantine ." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

However, the road to a sequel has been anything but smooth.

"We've been trying, and we've hit roadblock after roadblock," Lawrence says. "The character was given to somebody to make a network television show, which I never watched, and I don't think it lasted long." He continues, "Then J.J. [Abrams] somehow had the rights, or control of the character, for a while and was going to do something with Constantine . But he switched over, and he's now involved in our project too. He's a great guy, and he's pro making this Constantine movie, which is fantastic.".

The other obstacle, Lawrence says, is "there were new people running DC with their own plans for the characters."

Though he doesn't name anyone, Lawrence notes there has since been a regime change at DC. It was announced on Nov. 9 that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-CEOs of DC studios four years after taking the job. Skydance, which now oversees the division following the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, has appointed former Marvel exec Jeremy Latcham to the post of president and chief creative officer of DC Studios.

With new leadership in place, and with relationships of his own among the executives now running Warner Bros., Lawrence sees an opening. "Maybe there's some renewed hope to get Constantine through," he says.

"I'm a believer that we could make a sequel to our Constantine with Keanu, and if people at DC wanted to do a different version of Constantine in some sort of shared universe, they could do that, and the two could coexist." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Constantine isn't the only long-gestating project on his plate. With Sunrise now in theaters, Lawrence is also turning his attention to Red Rising , Pierce Brown's bestselling sci-fi book series, which he has been developing with the author, a friend, for about eight years.

Development of an adaptation first began as a series at Netflix, with two pilot scripts he calls "fantastic," but it stalled. "There's just regime changes, and it was an expensive buy-in for them," he says. "We kept getting shifted around to different departments."

"They never really pulled the trigger," he adds. "Now there's a renewed excitement because we're at Paramount and it's theatrical again. We have a screenwriter working on it, so I'm very excited."

All roads seemingly lead back to Panem, with Lawrence acknowledging how Red Rising can have a clear thread back to Hunger Games character Plutarch Heavensbee, the Gamemaker turned rebel played by Plemons in Sunrise and the late Philip Seymour Hoffman in the original films. "One of the things that I love about Plutarch is that Plutarch is a bit of an infiltrator," Lawrence says. Red Rising is an infiltration story too. The story follows Darrow, described as "a rebel forged by tragedy, battling to lead his oppressed people to freedom."

"It allows characters to really question themselves, cross weird moral boundaries and question the people around them. What happens when the people you hate suddenly become more relatable than some of the people that you're fighting for?" he says. "I've always been fascinated by those kinds of stories." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Also on deck is BioShock , an adaptation of 2K Games' 2007 first-person shooter. "We're doing a rewrite on a script now," Lawrence says. "I think that's getting closer and closer." In fact, he had a call about the project scheduled for shortly after his conversation with THR .

Thirteen years after the Hunger Games franchise began, the odds remain firmly in Panem's favor. In its opening weekend, Sunrise on the Reaping grossed $120 million , becoming its fourth-best debut in franchise history, besting 2015's second Mockingjay movie ($102.6 million) and 2023 prequel The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6 million) but behind 2013's Catching Fire ($158 million), 2012's series-launching The Hunger Games ($152.5 million) and 2014's first Mockingjay ($121.8 million).

For Lawrence, who has lived in this world for more than a decade, the prequels have done more than extend the franchise. They've changed how he understands it.

"Going through each of these books page by page with Suzanne over time has given me a pretty deep knowledge of the world and the lore. But now that she's writing these prequels and reframing characters, I'm also learning more each time she releases a book," he says.

He counts himself a fan, but perhaps not the biggest one on set. "I'm sure there are super fans, even people like Mckenna Grace [Maysilee Donner in Sunrise ], who is a super fan of these stories, who know more about all the little nooks and crannies than I do," he says with a laugh. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid10' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

After so many years of working side by side with Collins, the page and the screen have started to merge in his mind. "The lines between the book and the script start to blur, and you forget what's just in the movies and what's exactly from the book," he says.

Plenty of dystopian YA series followed in The Hunger Games ' wake, Divergent and The Maze Runner among them, but none has lasted the way Panem has. Lawrence credits Collins' finger on the pulse of the world as the reason for the story maintaining its popularity.

"Part of what originally separated these books from other YA publications: they had real meat on the bone thematically," Lawrence says of the story's lasting appeal. "She also created a world, a narrative and characters people fell in love with: Katniss, Peeta, Effie Trinket. But if they didn't have the ideas underneath them, they would feel a bit empty and surface-level, and they wouldn't land the same way. That's one of the things I feel really lucky about, honestly: we get to make movies that lots of people go to see, but that really have something to say about the world we live in. For me, that's why they endure."

Does telling this story in today's climate feel different than it did when the original films came out? "A little bit," Lawrence says. But the ideas, he argues, have always been built to last.

"Suzanne's original inspiration was watching war footage, then switching channels and seeing reality game shows, and she decided to write this series about the consequences of war for teens. Whether Collins has more to say in Panem is a question only she can answer. In the meantime, the world she built keeps showing up in the real one. articles.title: I Don't Think Enough People Talk About What A Masterpiece From The '90s 12 Monkeys Is
articles.summary: Pulp Fiction is great and all, but what about 12 Monkeys?!
articles.content:
When discussing movies from the ‘90s, there are some films that get mentioned all the time. I'm talking about movies like Pulp Fiction , The Silence of the Lambs , and, of course, The Shawshank Redemption (Even though I think it's just “good” and not great).

However, do you want to know what movie ISN’T on our list? The 1995 masterpiece (Yes, masterpiece) 12 Monkeys . I actually think it’s one of the best films from that decade, and here’s why.

A lot of people like to bring up great opening scenes in films , but do you know what I don’t think gets enough credit? Great opening songs, and look, I get it. Many older, typically black-and-white films (or westerns!) began with opening credits and stirring music before we met the characters. But nowadays, most films jump right into the action (in medias res, as it were).

I love a good time travel story , and 12 Monkeys has one of my favorites of any film. The story concerns a convict named Cole (Bruce Willis) who is sent back in time to investigate what caused the virus that killed 99% of the human population. He’s tasked with learning who the “Army of the 12 Monkeys” are, since they’re suspected of releasing the virus, as there are records of them writing, “We did it!”

Lastly, Brad Pitt is just so good in this movie. He plays a mental asylum patient, and the closest thing I can compare his performance to is Johnny Depp wigging out in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas .

articles.title: 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way’s Ally Claps Back After Parents Say Show Faked Their Pregnancy Reaction
articles.summary: There's an added layer to the drama.
articles.content:
90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way 's Ally Yahuff and her family are currently embroiled in some drama due to a recent episode. Ally's parents claimed the show scripted their daughter's pregnancy reveal scene . However, the TLC star is now pushing back. As her storyline continues to unfold on the 2026 TV schedule , Ally is suggesting that the only fake element is her parents' latest public response.

Ally's stress makes sense, considering the circumstances. Those who assumed the scene was faked may also assume that her crying in bed after the scene wasn't genuine, and that makes the whole situation seem very dramatic and silly. Additionally, past cast members have claimed 90 Day is faked , and I can imagine it'd feel really rough to have the internet decide a real-life traumatic event was just scripted television.

Once again, 90 Day Fiancé fans keeping up with the 2026 TV schedule are caught in the game of "he said, she said." Like what happened with the drama surrounding Vittorio Palchetti's house not being his actual home, it feels like there's an explanation for all of this. Yet, because the audience was misled from the start, I can't help but feel skeptical of everything.

On the one hand, I can imagine that parents who would disown their adult child for an unexpected pregnancy would also feel ashamed about being called out for it later. Conversely, Ally was very clearly showing ahead of their big reveal, to the point that I'm not sure it was even necessary for Jonathan to state it.

Marvel boss Kevin Feige has already made it clear that a full reboot of the MCU is off the table, calling the changes after Secret Wars more like a "reset."

Speaking in a new interview with Entertainment Weekly , Feige opened up about how Doomsday and Secret Wars will interact with the MCU's future after they're released, calling this year's film “a culmination of what’s come before" and adding that Secret Wars "will very much be a launching pad for our films in 2028 — the 20th anniversary of the MCU — and launching a very new era at that point.” That new era has a firm foundation too: The X-Men.

Avengers: Secret Wars may be the only MCU movie currently scheduled to be released in 2027, but Marvel has already confirmed what films will be released in 2028, all of which reveal what the future of the franchise looks like. May of 2028 will kick off with X-Men , followed by Ryan Gosling's Ghost Rider in July and Black Panther III in December. These three films paint a clear picture of how the MCU is not only building on what came before it, but springing forth into all-new territory, and the X-Men being first out of the gate is no coincidence.

"The X-Men are extremely important,” Feige told the outlet. “You can’t underestimate it. When you look at the comics, other than Avengers and Spider-Man, there’s almost nothing more important. We talk about it in terms of sagas, because there are so many amazing sagas within the X-Men comics over the past 60 years. The potential to continue our film series is almost limitless now that we have access to the X-Men.”

Though what's in store for the MCU after the three movies confirmed for 2028 has yet to be confirmed, it's an easy guess to make that the X-Men characters won't be confined to their own movies and could be the building blocks that keep audiences engaged and let the MCU tell new stories. Feige has already made it clear that the MCU's take on the X-Men, only possible now thanks to Disney acquiring 20th Century Fox, will delve in to storylines and characters from the decades of X-Men comics that haven't had their time in the spotlight (meaning a third try for Dark Phoenix seems unlikely)

As Feige rightfully pointed out, the X-Men offer the MCU enough stories, characters, and teams to fill up years of movies and TV shows. On top of the mainline team, characters like Wolverine will no doubt show up down the line, and the potential for the likes of X-Force, Excalibur, Alpha Flight, and X-Factor seems more likely than ever.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Carrie has been a success for Amazon Prime Video, defying the odds to deliver a compelling modern update to Stephen King's classic coming-of-age horror story and Brian De Palma's equally classic 1976 film adaptation. Then again, it shouldn't be surprising that Carrie (2026) did as well as it did: showrunner Mike Flanagan ( Midnight Mass, The Haunting of Hill House , Clayface ) has been on a tear the last few years, becoming one of the most acclaimed voices in horror-drama films and TV shows.

Traditionally, Prime Video launches its original series in binge-watch format, then tallies the performance data to see if another season is a viable option; it took Carrie less than two weeks to earn a Season 2 renewal , as viewers not only showed up to watch but also loved the series and its expansion on Stephen King's lore. But when is Carrie Season 2 going to premiere? Today we have an update – but it's probably not the one that fans were hoping for.

Mike Flanagan did some in-depth dissection of his Carrie series with THR . During the chat, Flanagan went into where things stand with Carrie Season 2 and its production timeline. Long story short? The series won't start filming the sophomore season until sometime next year. That means it won't be ready to air until sometime in 2028, at the earliest.

"I turned in the first episode script earlier this morning, which is very exciting," Flanagan said in his update. "We’ve been working on it unofficially for a while because I had always hoped that it could go this way and wanted to be prepared in case it did. We’re gearing up to hopefully go into production next year, and we’ll see how it all shapes up."

That's actually a pretty good middle ground for most modern high-concept TV shows like Carrie : In some cases, planning for additional seasons doesn't even begin until there's an official greenlight. Between planning and production, that's where you see 2-3 year gaps that can really cost a show fans; Apple TV's breakout hits Severance and Pluribus are both timely examples of this.

In the case of Carrie , having a plan in place is key; Season 2 will take Flanagan's adaptation beyond the pages of Stephen King's writing, with Carrie White (Summer H. Howell) ( SPOILERS !) escaping her town and her high school nightmare to discover her place in a long line of extraordinary gifted women.

"The beautiful thing is that Carrie’s journey has always seemed to me to have a clear trajectory. And that was something, even though we were never taking for granted that it would happen, it was something that was always in the back of my mind. I know it was in conversations that I had with Summer about where she could go and with Steve too — King was very aware and excited about the potential for that," Flanagan said. "It’s always been in the room with us, but we didn’t really have permission to fully explore it until it was real because you don’t want to jinx it. But we are fully immersed in it. The writers' room is firing on all cylinders."

With Season 1 setting up an entire cult of psychically-powered women, and Carrie on a road trip trying to avoid them, there is already plenty of intrigue for both episodic stops along the way an da continuining overarching story.

Prime Video's Carrie is currently developing Season 2.

articles.title: The Millennium Falcon Is Great but These 5 Star Wars Ships Are the Coolest of Them All
articles.summary: Star Wars looked very different from the other sci-fi we had seen before 1977. In the '50s and '60s, the Golden Age of Sci-Fi, we pictured clean, orderly, high-tech futures, but Star Wars went a different direction. While there was more than its share of sleek, modern tech, most of it was used, "lived-in", beaten […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars looked very different from the other sci-fi we had seen before 1977. In the '50s and '60s, the Golden Age of Sci-Fi, we pictured clean, orderly, high-tech futures, but Star Wars went a different direction. While there was more than its share of sleek, modern tech, most of it was used, "lived-in", beaten up like '70s America. The best example of this is the Millennium Falcon . Known as the "fastest hunk of junk in the galaxy", Han Solo and Chewbacca's YT-1300 light freighter was heavily modified, with souped-up engines, military-grade shields, armor, and weapons, and a specialized computer system to run it all (I say, computer, but in canon and Legends, it's actually a bunch of droid brains rigged together).

It was the first personal ship we saw in Star Wars , but it wouldn't be the last. Over the years, in both canon and Star Wars Legends , we've seen all kinds of awesome ships, owned by the best pilots and modified to high heaven. As great as the Falcon is, there are some ships that are way cooler, including these five designs from canon and Legends.

People love to compare Star Wars canon to Legends , but it's honestly kind of a boring comparison. Both have their high points (as I'll try to illustrate at various places) and one of the highest points for both was the first Thrawn Trilogy. These three books – Heir to the Empire, Dark Force Rising, and The Last Command – introduced numerous amazing characters, including the smuggler Talon Kardde. Kardde built up a massive illegal empire under everyone's noses and had a small fleet of smuggler vessels, including the Wild Kardde . A modified Corellian Engineering Corporation Action VI Bulk Freighter, it was a very unique vessel and the flagship of his fleet, alongside the Etherway and the Starry Ice .

To begin with, it was a massive bulk freighter, meaning that Kardde and crew could hide just about anything in its cavernous holds. It had a very powerful power plant, allowing Kardde to give the ship military-grade weapons, shields, and sensors. It had thick armor and was armed with three turbolasers, each of them hidden in the hull until needed. It could shoot it out with the big ships, could run from the fastest chase craft, and looked so assuming it could go anywhere. It's a favorite of many Legends fans.

Disney's tenure in control of Lucasfilm gets a bad rep, but it has introduced some amazing Star Wars characters over the years, including the incomparable Din Djarin, the Mandalorian. Din has had quite a journey over the course of the series, one that started out with the Razor's Crest . I'm an old school Legends fan and I loved the Razor's Crest immediately. It had just the right feel and look for a bounty hunter ship. It looked like a standard freighter, lightly armed, and nondescript, exactly the kind of ship you'd see anywhere.

Manufactured by the Corellian Engineering Corporation and Belsmuth Consolidations Ltd., it was a ST-70 M-111 Razor Crest series. Djarin souped up the engines and cannons, making it faster than it looked and letting it pack a stronger punch, and it had a cool look to it. It did end up getting destroyed by the Empire on Tython, but he'd get another one. It helped give The Mandalorian that Legends feel that really did it for me in the show's beginning.

The '90s were a better time than they seemed to be a Star Wars fan. Sure, there was no movies or TV shows, but there were books, comics, toys, role-playing games, and video games. In 1996, we got the multimedia project Star Wars: Shadow of the Empire , which consisted of a novel, comics, RPG supplements, toys, and a N64 video game. It introduced several cool new characters including Dash Rander, a Corellian smuggler. He was basically a Han wannabe – the story took place between Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi , so he was frozen in carbonite and the story needed a scoundrel – down to his souped Corellian freighter, the Outrider .

It was a YT-2400, a newer generation than the Falcon . It was almost as fast in hyperspace, but faster at sublight, and had powerful shields and weapons, including two double laser turrets and concussion missile launchers. It was basically the Falcon if it was better kept up and has more than its share of fans. It also appeared in the Special Edition of Episode IV in 1997, so it's technically canon.

Mara Jade is the great lost Legends character . Fans have wanted her brought into canon even if she can't marry Luke Skywalker for years now. The former Emperor's Hand was a powerful Force using assassin before she met Luke. He brought her to the light and she eventually trained as a Jedi, marrying him at the end of the war against the Empire. The two of them led the New Jedi Order through the Yuuzhan Vong War and the Joiner War, but she'd end killed in the Second Galactic Civil War. In the last few years of her life, she flew the Jade Shadow , a SoroSuub Horizon -class star yacht.

It was heavily modified, with powerful shields and engines. It was armed with retractable laser cannons, a retractable blaster cannon, concussion missile launchers, and a tractor beam projector. Jade had the ship specially designed for her, with a special cockpit that would allow her to control every station herself from the helm. Jade was one of the best pilots in the galaxy, so the Jade Shadow handled like a starfighter despite being 55 meters long. She was fast and powerful, an amazing ship for an amazing woman.

Star Wars: Skeleton Crew was an underrated gem and it's the type of show that shows that we shouldn't just give up on canon, even if we get lackluster stuff like The Acolyte or The Mandalorian and Grogu . The show followed a group of children who found a hidden pirate chip and fly into the stars, on the course of adventure. It was basically Goonies meets Star Wars and it's fantastic. That ship is the Onyx Cinder . It was a vessel that was commissioned years ago by the Galactic Republic, one of its treasury ships meant to transport credit ingots from the Republic mint on At Attin.

It was stolen by pirates at some point before the fall of the Republic, used by captains like Tak Rennod and Jod Na Nawood. It was everything you could want from pirate ship – it was fast, durable, and it had a secret, as its hull was just an armored sleeve for the real Onyx Cinder . I loved this ship from the second I saw it. It just looks awesome. It's the kind of ship that anyone would want to command – fast, durable,and powerful – with a cool secret that hides an even better design.

What Star Wars ships do you like more the Millennium Falcon ? Or do you think it can't be topped? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The latest Nintendo GameCube game on Nintendo Switch Online has now arrived on the subscription platform. Throughout 2026, Nintendo has slowly been bringing classic GameCube titles to Switch Online for those who happen to own a Switch 2. While this GameCube library is still pretty slim, it contains some of the all-time best games that appeared on the platform such as The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker , Luigi's Mansion , Super Mario Sunshine , and Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance . Now, Nintendo has added its 12th game to this growing lineup of GameCube titles on NSO, and it's one that subscribers weren't anticipating.

Starting today, Wave Race: Blue Storm is available to play via Nintendo Switch Online's GameCube catalog. Released in November 2001, Wave Race: Blue Storm is primarily synonymous with the GameCube as it was a launch game for the platform. As the sequel to the N64 classic Wave Race 64 , Blue Storm features roughly the same gameplay as its predecessor, with players racing jetskis against one another across a variety of different maps.

Although it might not be as popular as Wave Race 64 , Blue Storm was still plenty popular amongst GameCube owners. As a result, it's addition to Nintendo Switch Online is very much a welcome one to those subscribed at the Expansion Pack tier of the service.

"Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001," says the game's description. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms. Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!"

While it's a very nice surprise to see Wave Race: Blue Storm now available through Nintendo Switch Online, it does continue to raise one big question. Specifically, Nintendo previously announced well over a year ago that Pokemon Colosseum would be coming to NSO in the future. Instead, Nintendo's latest two additions to this GameCube library, Star Fox Adventures and now Wave Race: Blue Storm , were ones that it previously didn't reveal would be coming to the subscription platform. For these games to have arrived prior to Pokemon Colosseum is a bit odd and only raises further questions about when this Pokemon spin-off might become available.

The good news is that Nintendo hasn't announced that Pokemon Colosseum is no longer planned to join Nintendo Switch Online. As a result, it might simply be waiting for the right opportunity to pull the trigger. With Pokemon Day set to take place in February 2027, perhaps we'll see the GameCube classic added to Switch Online around this time.

Until then, what do you think about Wave Race: Blue Storm joining NSO today? Are you going to look to play this returning classic for yourself? Be sure to let me know down in the comments.
